## Installing R and RStudio {#installing-r-and-rstudio}

You **must** have R and RStudio installed on your laptop before the second class session (ideally before the first). Both are free.

### Step 1 — Install R

**Windows:**

1. Go to <https://cran.r-project.org/>
2. Click *Download R for Windows* → *base* → *Download R-x.x.x for Windows*
3. Open the installer and follow the prompts (accept defaults)

**Mac:**

1. Go to <https://cran.r-project.org/>
2. Click *Download R for macOS*
3. Select the most recent `.pkg` file **for your Mac's chip** (Apple silicon vs. Intel — check  → About This Mac)
4. Open the `.pkg` file and follow the prompts

### Step 2 — Install RStudio

1. Go to <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>
2. Click *Download* under **RStudio Desktop (Open Source Edition)**
3. Select your operating system, run the installer, accept defaults

### Step 3 — Test your installation

Open RStudio. In the Console (bottom-left), type:

```r
2 + 2
```

Press Enter. If you see `[1] 4`, you're ready.

### Step 4 — Install the course packages

Paste this into the Console and press Enter (it takes a few minutes):

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "swirl", "BayesFactor", "here", "modeest"))
```

(`modeest` is small but easy to miss — Homework 2 and the mid-term use it to find the mode. A few later packages — `brms`, `emmeans`, `correlation`, `car` — are staged in the weeks that need them; each week's session page tells you what to install.)

### Troubleshooting

- If RStudio won't open, make sure R is installed *first* — RStudio requires it.
- If you get a message about an outdated R version, install the newest R, then restart RStudio.
- Still stuck? See the [R installation FAQ](https://cran.r-project.org/faq.html) or email me — *before* class, not the night homework is due.

## Datasets

Download by clicking, or read directly in R. `read_csv()` comes from the **tidyverse**, so load it first — once per R session, before any of the lines below:

```r
library(tidyverse)

prisoners <- read_csv("https://smourtgos.github.io/crju705/data/prisoners.csv")
```

(If you get `could not find function "read_csv"`, that's the missing `library(tidyverse)`.)

| File | Description | Used in |
|------|-------------|---------|
| [chicago-crimes-2025.csv](data/chicago-crimes-2025.csv) | **Anchor dataset**: 30,000 real Chicago crime incidents from 2025 — [full codebook](chicago-data.qmd) | Lectures, all semester |
| [chicago-areas.csv](data/chicago-areas.csv) | **Anchor dataset**: all 2025 Chicago crime aggregated to 77 community areas + ACS covariates — [full codebook](chicago-data.qmd) | Lectures (correlation → regression) |
| [prisoners.csv](data/prisoners.csv) | 300 incarcerated persons: demographics, offense type, sentence, stress/depression/sleep measures (simulated) | Lab 2 |
| [neighborhoods.csv](data/neighborhoods.csv) | 500 neighborhoods: poverty, unemployment, disorder level, assaults (simulated) | Lab 3 |
| [cities-wide.csv](data/cities-wide.csv) | 100 cities with violent-crime rates 2015–2025 in wide format (simulated) | Lab 4 |
| [reentry-wide.csv](data/reentry-wide.csv) | 150 reentry program participants, monthly outcomes in wide format (simulated) | Lab 4 |
| [population-data.csv](data/population-data.csv) | A full "population" of test scores for sampling-distribution simulations | Session 4 |
| [crash-ak.csv](data/crash-ak.csv) | 20,000 Alaska traffic-crash incidents: causes, severity, intoxication flags (simulated) | Lab 5, Workshop |
| [crash-ak.xlsx](data/crash-ak.xlsx) | The same crashes as a (messier) Excel file — for import practice | Lab 5 |
| [officers.csv](data/officers.csv) | 200 corrections officers: shift, tenure, overtime, burnout, PTSD screen (simulated) | Lab 6 |

The two **Chicago anchor files are real data** (Chicago Police Department portal + Census/ACS via CMAP) — see the [full codebook and caveats](chicago-data.qmd). The remaining datasets are simulated but realistic, generously shared by a colleague.

## The simulation verbs, in plain language {#simulation-verbs}

Every simulation in this course is built from a tiny vocabulary. When code looks dense, translate it with this table:

| Verb | Reads as | First appears |
|---|---|---|
| `sample(x, size, replace)` | "run one random event" — draw `size` values from `x` | Session 3 |
| `replicate(k, expr)` | "repeat the whole recipe `k` times and collect the answers" | Session 3 |
| `rbinom(n, size, prob)` | "flip `size` coins and count the successes — done `n` times" | Session 3 |
| `\(x) ...` | an *anonymous function*: "a mini-recipe with slot `x`" | Sessions 3–4 |
| `map_dbl(v, \(x) ...)` | "for each element of `v`, run the recipe; return one **number** each" — `replicate()`, tidyverse-flavored | Session 4 |
| `map(v, \(x) ...)` | same, but each result can be a whole object — results arrive as a **list column** | Session 4 |
| `list_rbind(l)` | "stack a list of small tibbles into one tibble" | Session 5 |
| `expand_grid(a = ..., b = ...)` | "every combination of these values, as rows" | Session 4 |
| `set.seed(705)` | "start the random-number generator at a fixed spot, so results reproduce" | everywhere |

Two idioms worth naming once:

- **The thousand-times pattern:** `tibble(draw = 1:1000) |> mutate(stat = map_dbl(draw, \(d) ...))` — "do it 1,000 times, keep every answer in a column." This powers most figures in Sessions 4–6.
- **List columns:** `s = map(draw, \(d) sample(...))` makes a column where each cell holds an *entire sample*. You never need to write one from scratch in this course — you only need to read past it and watch what's computed from it.

## Getting help

- **In this order:** R's built-in help (`?mean`), the R4DS [Getting Help chapter](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-help.html), a classmate, then me.
- **Office hours are on request** — email me and we'll set a time (virtual or in person), usually within a day or two. Don't sit stuck for days; that is exactly what the appointment is for.
- AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) are welcome as *collaborators* — see the [syllabus AI policy](syllabus.qmd#use-of-artificial-intelligence-tools) — but you must be able to explain every line you submit.
